title: Console aggregation hotpath: observability additions and systematic tech-debt paydown
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem statement: Console API aggregation and a set of GraphQL resolvers continue to contribute disproportionate 95th/99th percentile latency during dashboard load, driven by cross-service fanout, coarse-grained in-memory caches, and an aging dependency surface (apollo-server v2 -> v3 fragmentation, custom global cache singletons). This ticket coordinates a focused tech-debt paydown to reduce tail latency, add observability, and create safer refactor patterns for future changes.

Goals: 
- Reduce 99p latency for dashboard/collection pages by >=30% under production traffic profile.
- Replace brittle global in-memory caches with sharded cache adapters and introduce explicit cache lifecycle hooks.
- Upgrade critical GraphQL-related deps (apollo-server, graphql-tools) and eliminate deprecated resolver patterns.
- Add end-to-end tracing and aggregation-level SLI dashboards to detect regressions during rollouts.

Success metrics: 
- 99th p95/p99 for aggregation endpoint from 1.2s -> <=0.85s on Canary traffic.
- Error rate for aggregation requests <0.5% post-rollout.
- Integration test coverage for aggregator coercion logic >85%.

Plan / Workstreams: 
1) Observability baseline (week 1): add per-resolver tracing tags, measure KV cache hit/miss, and instrument fanout counts. Dashboards: aggregation latency heatmap, per-resolver histograms, prefix-cache miss surface.
2) Cache adapter refactor (week 2): extract global cache singletons to CacheAdapter interface; implement sharded Redis-backed adapter and an in-memory LRU with clear lifecycle for tests. Add metrics: cache.get.latency, cache.hits, cache.evictions.
3) Resolver flattening and async prefetch (week 2-3): move heavy remote lookups to an async prefetch pipeline that runs before the critical render path; convert blocking resolver chains into data loaders where appropriate.
4) Dependency upgrades (week 3): upgrade apollo-server v2 -> v3 compatible subset, bump graphql to 16.x, and consolidate data-loader libraries. Run smoke tests and fix deprecation breaks.
5) Canary rollout + throttled traffic (week 4): deploy to 1% traffic with additional tracing; run traffic replay for 48h; monitor dashboards and abort on regression.

Risks / Mitigations: 
- Upgrading apollo-server can change resolver execution order — mitigation: run integration test harness and synthetic trace replay before canary.
- Changing cache semantics could temporarily increase origin calls — mitigation: run pre-populate job to warm caches and keep a read-through fallback.

Artifacts & links: 
- Design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/aggregation-hotpath-observability
- Profiling capture (2026-02-08): https://internal-storage.redwood.ai/profiles/console-agg-2026-02-08-heap.html
- Draft PRs: github.com/redwood/console/pull/5412 (cache-adapter), github.com/redwood/console/pull/5429 (prefetch-pipeline), github.com/redwood/console/pull/5455 (deps-upgrade)
- Load replay job: gs://redwood-replays/console-agg-2026-02-26.json

Integration tests & QA: 
- Add integration scenario that runs full GraphQL query against local aggregated fixtures; assert per-field timings and cache metrics.
- Add chaos test to simulate an increased fanout with 50% of downstream calls delayed to 600ms.

Rollout plan: 
- Merge behind feature flag. Canary @ 1% for 48h with synthetic traffic + 2 real-customer sessions. If stable, increase to 10% for 24h, then 50% for 12h, and full rollout. Create automated rollback on 99p increase >20% or error-rate >0.5% within rollout window.

Longer-term follow-ups (not in scope for this ticket): 
- Move aggregation hotpath to a sidecar worker (future ticket to decouple blocking compute).
- Explore adaptive batching in the aggregation layer for variable traffic patterns.

Estimated effort: 8 points (2 devs x 2 weeks parallel work between cache adapter and resolver changes).
